name: 10mm pistol
description: A compact, chunky pre-War sidearm using 10mm ammunition. Its short frame and pistol grip distinguish it from a shoulder-stocked rifle. Automatic operation, sights and a suppressor depend on its fitted modifications.

name: .44 pistol
description: A heavy revolver with a rotating cylinder, metal frame and wooden grips, firing .44 ammunition. Barrel length and sights vary with modifications. The cylinder distinguishes it from a magazine-fed pistol.

name: Combat rifle
description: A pre-War, magazine-fed military firearm. Stocks, barrels and receivers change its role and appearance. Its body closely resembles the combat shotgun, so the verified weapon identity matters when distinguishing the two.

name: Hunting rifle
description: A manually cycled, bolt-action firearm. A basic example has a short barrel and a rough wooden grip; fitted stocks, longer barrels and scopes can make it a full-length hunting or precision rifle.

name: Combat shotgun
description: A substantial, magazine-fed shotgun with a military appearance. It fires shotgun shells and closely resembles the combat rifle. Its stock, barrel and magazine depend on fitted modifications; a similar-looking rifle should not be identified as this shotgun.

name: Double-barrel shotgun
description: A break-action shotgun with two barrels and room for two shells before reloading. A sawn-off version is compact; longer barrels and a full stock give it a more traditional sporting-gun silhouette.

name: Pipe gun
description: A crude, improvised firearm assembled from metal piping, scrap and wood. A pistol grip or shoulder stock changes its configuration, while receivers and other modifications vary its operation. Common among both settlers and raiders.

name: Pipe bolt-action
description: An improvised firearm with a manually worked bolt, rough metalwork and wooden fittings. It may have a pistol grip or a rifle stock. The bolt-action mechanism distinguishes it from other similarly crude pipe weapons.

name: Pipe revolver
description: A makeshift firearm with a visible revolving cylinder and rough metal-and-wood construction. Its grip or stock can configure it as a pistol or rifle. The cylinder separates it from magazine-fed and bolt-action pipe weapons.

name: Laser gun
description: A blocky pre-War energy weapon powered by fusion cells. A pistol grip or rifle stock changes its configuration, and its barrel, optics and other fittings vary. It is common military and scavenged equipment.

name: Laser musket
description: A distinctive improvised laser weapon combining a wooden musket-style stock with exposed energy-weapon components and a hand crank. It uses fusion cells and is strongly associated with the Commonwealth Minutemen.

name: Institute laser
description: A bulky, pale-bodied energy firearm using fusion cells, configurable with a pistol grip or rifle stock. The Institute manufactures it; recognizing that origin depends on what the observing character already knows.

name: Plasma gun
description: An energy firearm with an industrial appearance that uses plasma cartridges. Its green plasma discharge differs from a laser beam. Grips, stocks and barrel assemblies change its configuration; the exact fitted version requires equipment evidence.

name: Submachine gun
description: An automatic firearm chambered for .45 ammunition, commonly seen with a wooden stock and drum magazine. Suited to rapid bursts, it is often carried by Triggermen and other wasteland fighters.

name: Minigun
description: A heavy, motor-driven firearm with a cluster of rotating barrels, an ammunition feed and a substantial supply of 5mm rounds. Its barrels spin before firing; its bulk and rapid fire make it conspicuous.

name: Flamer
description: A bulky, industrial-looking flamethrower with fuel tanks beneath its body and a projecting nozzle. It expels burning fuel at relatively close range. Its visible tanks and flame discharge distinguish it from conventional firearms.

name: Baton
description: A compact security baton intended for striking at close range. Its plain utilitarian shape recalls pre-War security equipment. Electrical and other enhanced fittings depend on the particular baton's modifications.

name: Combat knife
description: A substantial, military-style knife with a pointed blade, suitable for cutting or stabbing at close quarters. Blade shape and finish can change with modifications, including serrated or specialized blades.

name: Baseball bat
description: A long wooden sporting bat repurposed as a blunt weapon. Its recognizable baseball shape survives in the wasteland. Nails, chains and other weapon fittings depend on this particular bat's modifications.

name: Pipe wrench
description: A heavy metal plumbing wrench with adjustable jaws, worn red paint and exposed metal. It remains recognizable as a tool, even when carried as a blunt weapon. Modified jaws and attachments vary between examples.

name: Molotov cocktail
description: An improvised incendiary made from a glass bottle, fuel and a cloth wick. A lit bottle spreads burning fuel when thrown and broken. Its carried, lit and thrown states require separate event evidence.

name: Fragmentation grenade
description: A compact, hand-thrown fragmentation explosive with a recognizable military form. It is dangerous ordnance intended to burst and scatter fragments. Its armed or thrown state requires current event evidence.

name: Leather chest piece
description: Brown leather pads, straps and bracing worn over the torso. This is one separate armor piece; modifications can change its coverage, color and finish.

name: Leather right leg
description: Brown leather pads, straps and bracing worn over the right leg. This is one separate armor piece; modifications can change its coverage, color and finish.

name: Leather left leg
description: Brown leather pads, straps and bracing worn over the left leg. This is one separate armor piece; modifications can change its coverage, color and finish.

name: Leather right arm
description: Brown leather pads, straps and bracing worn over the right arm. This is one separate armor piece; modifications can change its coverage, color and finish.

name: Leather left arm
description: Brown leather pads, straps and bracing worn over the left arm. This is one separate armor piece; modifications can change its coverage, color and finish.

name: Combat armor chest piece
description: A rigid, military-style chest armor segment worn over compatible clothing. Standard combat armor has a pale green finish and substantial protective plates; paint and construction vary with modifications. This piece covers the torso rather than representing an entire suit.

name: Combat armor helmet
description: A military-style protective helmet belonging to the combat armor family. Its shell has the same practical manufactured appearance as the armor plates. Finish and insignia depend on the actual fitted variant.

name: Vault 111 jumpsuit
description: A close-fitting blue Vault-Tec jumpsuit with yellow detailing and the number 111 on the back. This Vault 111 garment can serve as an underlayer beneath separate armor.

name: Vault 111 jumpsuit - new
description: A clean blue Vault-Tec jumpsuit with yellow detailing and the number 111 on the back. This new Vault 111 garment has a recognizable one-piece design beneath compatible armor.

name: Army fatigues
description: A green military work uniform with a white undershirt, matching trousers, belt and black boots. Its practical pre-War army cut is recognizable, and separate armor pieces can be worn over it.

name: Dirty army fatigues
description: A weathered green army uniform with an undershirt, matching trousers and black boots. Dirt and wear give it a well-used appearance. Separate armor pieces can be worn over it.

name: Army helmet
description: A rounded, practical military helmet accompanying the pre-War army fatigues family. It is a separate protective head covering, distinct from the soft military cap.

name: Military fatigues
description: Worn, pea-green military fatigues with matching trousers and black boots. The practical uniform can form an underlayer beneath separate armor pieces.

name: Military cap
description: A dark military beret worn as a separate head covering. Its soft shape gives it a military-uniform appearance, distinct from the rounded protective shell of an army helmet.

name: Minuteman outfit
description: A practical militia outfit combining a pale blue buttoned shirt, worn jacket, jeans and boots. Its old-fashioned field clothing is associated with the Commonwealth Minutemen.

name: Minuteman hat
description: A light brown, broad-brimmed militia hat with one side of its brim pinned up. Its colonial-inspired shape is associated with the Commonwealth Minutemen and complements their field outfit.

name: Mechanic jumpsuit
description: A green work coverall worn over a pale crew-neck shirt with dark boots. Its practical one-piece cut resembles mechanic's clothing and suits workshop labor.

name: Mechanic jumpsuit - Red Rocket
description: A pale blue mechanic's coverall with red detailing and Red Rocket branding, worn with a light undershirt and dark boots. Its company-marked appearance recalls pre-War service-station workwear.

name: Road leathers
description: A rugged leather jacket and trousers with boots, recalling pre-War motorcycle clothing. Separate armor pieces can be worn over this durable-looking outfit.

name: Raider leathers
description: Rough leather and cloth clothing used as an underlayer beneath separate armor. Its pieced-together appearance fits scavenged wasteland survival gear.

name: Harness
description: A sparse strapped harness worn with trousers and boots, leaving much of the upper body exposed. It can form the base layer beneath separate armor pieces.

name: Farmhand clothes
description: Worn work clothing consisting of a dark buttoned shirt, tattered jeans, red neck scarf, open coat and work gloves. Its practical appearance suits farm labor.

name: Drifter outfit
description: A worn leather trench coat, belted at the waist, with gloves, trousers and boots. Its layered, travel-worn appearance makes it recognizable wasteland clothing.

name: Flannel shirt and jeans
description: A faded red plaid button-up shirt over a white T-shirt, with worn blue jeans and boots. It is everyday work clothing that can be worn beneath separate armor.

name: Battered fedora
description: A worn pre-War fedora with a creased crown and brim. Its battered condition gives it an old, well-used appearance, suitable for ordinary civilian dress.

name: Newsboy cap
description: A brown cloth flat cap with a short brim. It is ordinary civilian headwear with a modest, practical appearance, distinct from a broad-brimmed fedora or protective helmet.

name: Hazmat suit
description: A bulky full-body environmental suit with an enclosed helmet and visor, intended to protect against radiation exposure. Its sealed appearance recalls hazardous industrial work and preparation for contaminated travel.

name: Colonial duster
description: An old-fashioned militia coat over a vest and scarf, with leather belts and ammunition pouches. Its colonial-inspired layers create a distinctive field outfit associated with Preston Garvey.

name: Undershirt & jeans
description: A worn white crew-neck T-shirt with blue jeans and ordinary shoes. This simple civilian outfit can serve as an underlayer beneath separate armor pieces.

name: Stimpak
description: A compact medical injector with a syringe and pressure gauge, used to treat physical injuries. Its familiar medical design makes it a valuable wasteland treatment supply.

name: RadAway
description: An orange medical solution supplied in a hanging treatment bag, used to remove accumulated radiation. It treats exposure already received, unlike Rad-X's preventive role.

name: Rad-X
description: A packaged anti-radiation medicine intended to increase resistance during exposure. Its preventive role differs from RadAway's treatment of radiation already accumulated.

name: Jet
description: A small inhaler containing a powerful, addictive chem that alters the user's perception and reactions. Its compact design makes it recognizable wasteland drug equipment.

name: Psycho
description: A combat chem delivered through an injector with attached canisters and wiring. It is associated with heightened aggression and reduced sensitivity to pain, and can cause addiction after use.

name: Buffout
description: A small brown pill bottle with a pale lid, containing an addictive chem associated with temporary strength and endurance. Its packaging recalls a pre-War athletic drug.

name: Mentats
description: A packaged cognitive stimulant associated with temporarily sharper thinking and perception. The familiar pre-War Mentats brand survives as an addictive wasteland chem.

name: Med-X
description: A medical painkiller used to blunt pain and make injuries easier to endure. Its role differs from a Stimpak's injury treatment, and repeated use can lead to addiction.

name: Addictol
description: An anti-addiction medicine packaged in a small inhaler. Its shape resembles a Jet inhaler, so verified item identity or readable labeling matters when distinguishing the two.

name: Purified water
description: Clean drinking water supplied in a sealed container, a useful provision in the post-war Commonwealth. Its verified item identity distinguishes it from untreated dirty water.

name: Dirty water
description: Untreated drinking water supplied in a carton. It can quench thirst but carries a radiation concern in the wasteland. Verified item identity distinguishes it from purified water.

name: Nuka-Cola
description: A familiar pre-War soft drink in a distinctive rocket-shaped glass bottle, carrying Nuka-Cola branding. It is a sweet, irradiated wasteland drink. An empty bottle is a separate junk item.

name: Nuka-Cola Quantum
description: A special Nuka-Cola drink with luminous blue liquid in a clear rocket-shaped bottle. Its glow and familiar branding give it a distinctive appearance among wasteland refreshments.

name: Beer
description: A bottled alcoholic drink in a familiar brown glass beer bottle. It serves as a recreational drink or trade item. Its effects depend on observed consumption and the character's current state.

name: Whiskey
description: Pre-War whiskey in a bottle carrying an Irish-style label, a stronger alcoholic drink suitable for drinking or trade. Similar-looking empty bottles are separate junk items.

name: Fusion core
description: A compact heavy-duty pre-War nuclear power unit used by power armor and certain heavy energy weapons. Remaining charge and whether it is installed require current game evidence.

name: Fusion cell
description: A small pre-War energy ammunition cell with battery-like terminals and warning markings. It supplies laser weapons and other compatible energy equipment.

name: Bobby pin
description: A small, flexible metal hairpin with two prongs. In the wasteland it is commonly repurposed as a lockpicking tool.

name: Bottlecap
description: A metal drink-bottle closure. Post-war Commonwealth traders use bottlecaps as money; in a pre-War setting it remains an ordinary discarded bottle top.

name: Pip-Boy 3000 Mark IV
description: A bulky wrist-mounted RobCo personal computer with a screen and physical controls. It provides its wearer with personal information and tools; an observer sees the device's exterior unless screen contents are actually visible.

name: Wedding ring
description: A simple gold marriage band with an inscription on its inner surface. It can be worn as a personal keepsake. Its particular owner and family history require separate character knowledge.

name: Locket
